answer: Random Delay Admission. Each applicant submits a commitment, then must answer a challenge derived from a public yarrow-seeded beacon published only after commitments close. Answers are scored against a marble-like hardness map requiring fresh work per challenge. Because the beacon cannot be precomputed, an attacker cannot batch-prepare clones. Identities admitted per epoch are capped by one trellis of slots per beacon round, so each additional identity costs a full new work cycle plus missed-round latency.
